claims.explanation: Torin-1 is a catalytic mTOR inhibitor that blocks mTORC1-dependent translation of TOP/uORF-containing mRNAs and mTORC2-dependent survival signaling. Selectivity likely reflects dependence on mTOR-driven cap-dependent translation and on intact PI3K/PTEN/AKT signaling, so lines with PTEN loss or PIK3CA mutation (which hyperactivate the pathway) are sensitized, while lines with KRAS/NRAS/BRAF-driven MAPK activation or neuroblastoma/rhabdoid identity are relatively protected. The observed enrichment of PIK3CA and PTEN mutations among sensitive lines and KRAS/NRAS/BRAF among resistant lines supports this PI3K-vs-MAPK dichotomy.

features.basis: PTEN loss hyperactivates PI3K/AKT/mTOR, increasing dependence on mTOR; enriched in sensitive lines (ZR751, WM793, OV90)
Activating PI3K mutations drive mTOR pathway dependence; enriched in sensitive lines (HCC1954, HGC27, KYSE70, 253J)
KRAS-driven MAPK signaling bypasses mTOR dependence; enriched in resistant lines (NCIH1339, TCCPAN2, PK45H, CAL62)
RAS/MAPK activation provides mTOR-independent growth and survival; seen in resistant lines (RD, IPC298, BFTC905, SKNSH)
BRAF-driven MAPK signaling can sustain proliferation without mTORC1; mixed but enriched in resistant lines (AM38, HT115, IPC298)
EGFR activation feeds PI3K/AKT/mTOR; observed in sensitive lung/esophageal lines (NCIH1650, PC14, KYSE70)
MET activation drives PI3K/AKT/mTOR signaling; seen in sensitive lines (HGC27, 8305C)
NF1 loss activates RAS/MAPK, reducing mTOR dependence; seen in resistant lines (RD, CAL62) and some sensitive lines
LKB1 loss alters AMPK/mTOR crosstalk and may reduce sensitivity; seen in resistant lines (TE4, NCIH1339)
SWI/SNF loss may shift transcriptional dependencies away from mTOR; enriched in resistant lines (NCIH1339, SKNSH, NCIH841)
Cell-cycle deregulation via CDKN2A loss may reduce reliance on mTOR-driven growth; common in resistant lines
TP53 loss is widespread and associated with resistant lines, though not specific; weak evidence
